findings.text: SCRUTINY POINT 1 (no free-form path) - CONFIRMED, provably no free-form path in this module. resolve_action is the only way a reference becomes an action and it is a pure dict.get on a validated whitelist key; require_action and bind_remedy_action have no fallback branch that could admit a non-whitelisted or free-form action (both return a fail-count and None/error on a miss). There is no string-eval, no shell interpretation, no getattr-dispatch, and no command-text field anywhere on the resolution path. The proposed_action carries an action REFERENCE + a parameters mapping only; W1's check_remedy independently rejects command/run/shell keys upstream. NG2 holds structurally, not by instruction.

SCRUTINY POINT 2 (digest binding unspoofable) - CONFIRMED. action_digest excludes exactly the 'review' key and hashes every other top-level field via json.dumps(sort_keys=True); I verified field-by-field that editing any non-review field changes the digest and editing the review block alone does not. Because unknown top-level fields are also hashed (not stripped), an added field cannot ride along uncovered. action_reviewed enforces the three-way conjunction (status reviewed AND verdict approved AND digest match) and a rejected-verdict-at-reviewed-status is refused as a contradiction. No field can be edited post-review without going stale.

SCRUTINY POINT 3 (risk floor / conservatism) - CONFIRMED and, in my judgment, CORRECT not over-strict. risk_floor returns critical for BOTH data_mutating and irreversible; validate_action refuses declared-rank < floor-rank. The plan's C2 text names data-mutating -> critical explicitly and permits raising any class; the spec's AC2 extends critical to irreversible. Treating an irreversible-but-non-data-mutating action as critical is a RAISE (allowed, never a lowering) and is the right call: irreversibility is precisely the property that warrants the two-key/critical treatment even absent data mutation, since an unwindable action is as dangerous as a data write. I would keep it.

SCRUTINY POINT 4 (parameter validation complete) - CONFIRMED. Every declared type (string/integer/number/boolean/enum) has a real constraint check; integer is discriminated from float (isinstance int) and bool is excluded from numeric coercion (_as_number rejects bool) so True cannot satisfy a numeric range; unknown/extra supplied parameters are REJECTED by name, not silently accepted, closing the vector where an accepted extra param reaches the future executor. String also enforces an optional max_length. Minor observation (non-blocking): a declared parameter pattern is validated to COMPILE at spec time and matched with re.fullmatch at value time; a pathological author-supplied pattern is a theoretical ReDoS surface, but the pattern is author-controlled repo content vetted through the same review as the action, not attacker-supplied, so it is not a live risk here.

SCRUTINY POINT 5 (the 'reviewed' state is self-declared) - CONFIRMED and this is THE residual trust the human approver is accepting. The review block (status, reviewer, verdict, reviewed_at, reviewed_digest) is data ON the artifact. The digest binding makes it TAMPER-EVIDENT (content cannot change post-review without going stale) but it does NOT PROVE that a genuine independent fresh-context review and a real human promotion produced that 'reviewed'/'approved' stamp. An author who computes the correct action_digest and writes status:reviewed/verdict:approved would pass action_reviewed. The store ENFORCES the recorded, digest-bound outcome; it does not PRODUCE it. This separation is honestly disclosed in the spec Out-of-scope ('No action review engine') and the shipped trio's review blocks are explicitly labeled 'illustrative fresh-context review (example only)'. What a human approving THIS spec vouches for is therefore the MECHANISM: (a) no whitelist reference can ever become command text (no free-form path), (b) 'reviewed' is digest-bound to exactly the reviewed content (no silent edit), (c) the risk floor cannot be talked down, (d) a bad or extra parameter is refused, by name, before any executor - all offline against fake systems. They are NOT yet vouching that a live review+promotion pipeline stamps the reviewed status (that is the loop plus human promotion, and the executor that would consume an admitted action is W6 / the two-key rule W7 - both honestly unbuilt). This is proportionate and correctly scoped for W5.

BONUS (byte-identity teeth). Both guard-mutation probes additionally tripped the AC5 byte-identity assertions (root action.py diverged from its plugin/templates and pack copies), independently confirming the engine-sync checks are themselves non-vacuous. No vacuous tests were found across AC1-AC5; every safety property I probed had a positive control and a mutation that turns a check red.
